steps.what: Check credit information on the applications.
Accept the applications information.
Record the accepted credit applications.
Accept the disbursements of funds.
Record the accepted disbursements.

tasks.design: The clerk checks the credit information and accepts the application, then {ERP} records that version. They accept a disbursement amount, and the record stores that version. The record does not release the funds. A treasury officer still moves the money.
tasks.previous_blocker: Applications and disbursements were keyed in, and a wrong amount was easy to post.
tasks.enabler_now: The loan screen can store fields the clerk has already accepted. It should be tried before a separate store is built.
tasks.still_hard: A disbursement amount still has to be accepted by the clerk, and releasing the money is not this task.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk accepts the application and the disbursement amount. The record stores those versions and does not pay.
tasks.altitude: The clerk still checks credit information and accepts both the application and the disbursement amount before either is recorded. Recording does not release funds.

reach.task: Move funds only after a disbursement the clerk accepted is on the record
reach.learn: The record is not the payment

evidence.claim: A loan screen can store an application and a disbursement amount the person already accepted. Storing the amount is not the release of the funds.

A decision on credit that has a legal effect on a person must not be taken by a system alone. A person decides. This design does not score an applicant, does not set a credit limit, and does not grant an extension.

assumptions: The workflow starts when an application or a disbursement is ready to record and ends when that accepted version is on the record. The clerk accepts both. The record does not pay.
The fields are the application items, the disbursement amount, and their acceptance. The clerk produces the acceptance. If an amount is blank, it is not recorded.
The prior classes this task as automate. The steps agree the keying of accepted fields can move. They disagree that a disbursement can be recorded before the clerk accepts the amount.
unknowns: Whether the loan screen can already store these fields.
Whether a second person must accept a disbursement before anyone pays it.
research_questions: Can the loan screen already store these fields?
Must a second person accept a disbursement before anyone pays it?

steps.what: Read the stated collateral value.
Check the collateral value against the security required.
Check whether that collateral can be held.
Note the collateral value they checked.

tasks.design: The clerk reads a collateral value someone else has already stated, then checks it against the security the loan requires and whether it can be held. They note that check. Nothing sets the lending value.
tasks.previous_blocker: The stated value was hunted for, and the check against the required security was done on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: A valuation already on the record can be opened. The check stays with the clerk.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the collateral is good security is still the clerk's check, not a model of the property.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk checks the value. They do not produce it.
tasks.altitude: The clerk still checks the collateral and whether it can be held. Reading a value that is already stated is the only part that moves.

reach.task: State the collateral value the clerk will check
reach.learn: The clerk does not replace the valuation

evidence.claim: A stated collateral value can be read. Checking it against the security required, and whether it can be held, stays with the person. A model does not set the lending value.

A decision on credit that has a legal effect on a person must not be taken by a system alone. A person decides. This design does not score an applicant, does not set a credit limit, and does not grant an extension.

assumptions: The workflow starts when a stated value is on the file and ends when the clerk has noted the check. They do not create the value.
The fields are the stated value and the security required. A valuer produces the value. The clerk produces the check. If no value is stated, they do not invent one.
The prior classes this task as human. The steps agree the check stays.
unknowns: Whether a valuer's figure is already on the loan file.
Who is allowed to state a collateral value.
research_questions: Is a valuer's figure already on the loan file?
Who is allowed to state a collateral value?

tasks.short: Contact customers about the recorded decision.

steps.what: Read the acceptance or rejection recorded.
Contact customers by telephone.
Contact customers in person.
Accept the applications letter of acceptance or rejection.
Send the accepted applications letter.

tasks.design: The clerk reads the acceptance or rejection already recorded, then contacts the customer by telephone or in person. A letter only restates that recorded decision. The clerk accepts the letter. {EMAIL} sends that version. The clerk does not make the decision, and the call is not recorded.
tasks.previous_blocker: The decision was read out, and a letter was typed from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: The decision, the amount, and the date can already be on the record, so a letter can restate those fields.
tasks.still_hard: The telephone call and the meeting stay, and a reason that is not on the record is not invented.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk contacts the customer and accepts a letter that only restates the recorded decision.
tasks.altitude: The calls and the meetings stay in full. The letter is sent only after the clerk accepts a version that restates the recorded decision and adds nothing.

reach.task: Hear the recorded decision from the clerk
reach.learn: The letter is not a new decision

evidence.claim: A letter can restate a decision, an amount, and a date that are already recorded. The call and the visit stay with the person. The letter does not decide the application.
Applicant financial data is personal data, used for the application the person is making. It is sent only in a version the clerk has accepted. National rules on credit references differ.

National rules differ on recording calls and on monitoring staff. This design does not record a call and does not score the clerk. A bot that spoke to a customer would have to say it is a machine. This design has no bot.

assumptions: The workflow starts when a decision is on the record and ends when the customer has been contacted. The clerk does not make the acceptance or the rejection. The call is not recorded.
The fields are the decision, the amount, and the date. Underwriting produces them. The clerk produces the acceptance of the letter. If a field is blank, that line is omitted.
The prior classes this task as human. The steps agree the contact stays. The letter only restates the record.
unknowns: Whether acceptance or rejection is already a field on the application.
Whether the customer has agreed to be contacted by mail.
research_questions: Is acceptance or rejection already a field on the application?
Has the customer agreed to be contacted by mail?

tasks.short: Prepare documents and file accepted checks.

steps.what: Prepare applications from accepted fields.
Prepare closing documents from those fields.
Prepare government notices from those fields.
Review checks and legal documents.
Accept the documents and the checks.
File the accepted documents and checks.

tasks.design: Standard forms are filled from application fields the clerk has already accepted, using the screen that already holds those forms where it can. The clerk reviews legal documents and checks, then accepts them. {DOCS} files that version. A treasury officer still signs any payment. Nothing drafts a legal term that was not in the fields.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same names and amounts were typed into each form and each check.
tasks.enabler_now: The loan screen's own forms should be tried first. A form can be filled from accepted fields.
tasks.still_hard: Legal wording that is not a field, and the signature on a check, stay with a person.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk reviews and accepts the documents and the checks. The file does not sign a payment.
tasks.altitude: The clerk still reviews legal documents and checks and accepts them before they are filed. The file is not a signature and not a payment.

reach.task: Sign a check the clerk prepared and accepted
reach.learn: The filed check is not a signature

evidence.claim: A form can be filled from names, amounts, and dates already accepted. Legal text that is not one of those fields, and the signature on a check, stay with a person.
Consumer-credit rules require a person to be able to intervene in an automated check of credit and to explain the result. Interest here is arithmetic on stated fields. It is not a credit decision.

assumptions: The workflow starts when an accepted application exists and ends when the accepted documents are on file. The clerk reviews checks and legal documents. Filing is not signing.

The fields are the name, the amount, the date, and their acceptance. The accepted application produces them. The clerk produces the acceptance of the document. If a form needs a sentence that is not a field, the clerk writes it.
The prior classes this task as automate. The steps agree the typing of accepted fields can move. They disagree that a check or a legal document can be filed before the clerk accepts it.
unknowns: Whether the loan screen already contains these forms.
Whether a second person must sign the check.
research_questions: Does the loan screen already contain these forms?
Must a second person sign the check?

role.altitude: The clerk still accepts an application and a disbursement amount before either is recorded, still checks collateral, still calls the customer, and still reviews checks and legal documents. Recording does not release funds. A letter only restates a decision already on the record.
reach: A treasury officer signs a check the clerk accepted
A customer hears a decision the record already holds
skills_to_grow: Accepting a disbursement amount before it is recorded
Checking a stated collateral value rather than setting one
Reviewing a legal document before it is filed
role.ambitious_version: Every disbursement that is recorded, and every document that is filed, is one the clerk accepted.
